newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: TRI to formalise German pact in Oct.
newsitem.headline: TRI to formalise German pact in Oct.

text.p: Malaysia's Technology Resources Industries Bhd (TRI) said on Thursday that it expects to formalise a previously-announced alliance with Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG in October 1996.

In a statement, the telecommunications concern also said that it will issue 68,071,332 new ordinary shares of the company at 9.25 ringgit a share. The price is lower than the 9.50 ringgit a share previously announced by TRI.
TRI also said that it has signed a management agreement and technical assistance and training agreement with Deutsche Telekom.

The company made the announcement about Deutsche Telekom amid rumours this week that the German fixed line services partner may want to pull out of the alliance or seek a cheaper price for its 21 percent stake purchase due to a decline in TRI's stock.
Signing of the agreement had been originally scheduled for Sept. 23.
TRI through its Cellular Communications Network Sdn Bhd operates Malaysia's largest cellular phone network. The company also has a fixed line network and an international phone service.
The tie-up with Deutsche Telekom is expected to help TRI expand its operations in Asia. Analysts have estimated the German firm's investment in TRI would cost over 1 billion ringgit.
Analysts said that the announcement went some way to clearing the air over recent rumours about the deal.

"TRI needs Deutsche Telekom," said a local telecommunications analyst. "So the fact that Deutsche are buying the new ordinary shares at 9.25 and not 9.50 as originally planned, is neither here nor there," he continued.
"It really has not come as too much of a surprise," said Haizan Khir Johari, telecommunications analyst at Schroders in Kuala Lumpur.

Under the original letter of intent signed on May 23, the issue price of the new shares was to have been reduced to 9.25 ringgit if TRI shares traded below 8.00 ringgit on a weighted average basis for any consecutive 14 calendar days up to Aug. 23.
The shares have been trading below 8.00 ringgit since late August. They ended at 6.80 ringgit on Thursday, up 50 cents.
